taxonomy.subtopic: C5b-C9 membrane attack complex formation and recurrent Neisseria infection

questions.stem_html: A 19-year-old college student is evaluated after a second episode of meningococcal bacteremia. Quantitative immunoglobulin levels and neutrophil oxidative-burst testing are normal. Serum C3 concentration is normal, but both classical- and alternative-pathway hemolytic screening assays show absent terminal lytic activity. The accompanying complement schematic ends before a transmembrane pore forms. Which function is most directly impaired?

options.text_html: Factor H-mediated inactivation of alternative-pathway C3 convertase
Polymerization of terminal complement components into a bacterial membrane pore
C1 inhibitor-mediated limitation of kallikrein activation

questions.explanation_html: Complement components C5b, C6, C7, C8, and polymerized C9 assemble the membrane attack complex, which creates pores in susceptible bacterial membranes. Deficiency of terminal components causes recurrent invasive Neisseria infections. Normal C3 helps preserve opsonization, whereas absent activity in both classical and alternative hemolytic screening assays localizes the defect to a shared terminal component.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: C3b opsonization depends on C3. A normal C3 concentration with the characteristic recurrent Neisseria pattern points instead to the terminal pathway.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: C5a is generated when C5 is cleaved and recruits neutrophils, but the defining defect described is failure of terminal pore formation.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: C1 inhibitor restrains the classical complement, contact, and kallikrein systems; its deficiency causes hereditary angioedema.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Factor H limits alternative-pathway activation on host surfaces. Deficiency predisposes to uncontrolled complement activation rather than isolated failure of terminal lysis.

questions.educational_objective: Terminal complement components C5b through C9 form the membrane attack complex; deficiency prevents bacterial membrane pore formation and predisposes to recurrent invasive Neisseria infection.

media.alt_text: Original complement cascade schematic showing convergence at C5 and assembly of C5b through C9 into a membrane attack complex pore.
